title: Four years, 28 moments
lede: From the first pitch to the last lawsuit. The service itself occupies eight months in the middle. Filter by thread.

events.title: Katzenberg pitches “NewTV”
events.text: A year after selling DreamWorks Animation, Katzenberg is on the cover of Variety promoting premium short-form video for phones, to be built by his holding company WndrCo.

events.title: Meg Whitman joins as CEO
events.text: Katzenberg calls Whitman on the day she announces her retirement from Hewlett Packard Enterprise; she signs on a few weeks later.

events.title: $1 billion raised
events.text: The first round is led by Madrone Capital Partners. Disney, NBCUniversal, Sony, Viacom, WarnerMedia, Lionsgate, MGM, ITV, Entertainment One and Alibaba all invest.

events.title: NewTV becomes Quibi
events.text: The name, short for “quick bites,” is announced at the Vanity Fair New Establishment Summit in Los Angeles.

events.title: First-year advertising sold out
events.text: Quibi says it has $150 million in commitments from advertisers including Google, P&G and PepsiCo.

events.title: CES keynote: Turnstyle, prices, launch date
events.text: $4.99 a month with ads, $7.99 without, launching April 6 with more than 175 shows and 8,500 episodes promised in year one.

events.title: Super Bowl LIV ad
events.text: “Bank Heist” is Quibi’s first national advertisement. USA Today’s Ad Meter ranks it fourth from bottom of 62.

events.title: $750 million second round
events.text: Upsized from $500 million. Total raised reaches $1.75 billion. Investors in the round are not named.

events.title: Quibi and Eko sue each other
events.text: Eko claims Turnstyle was built on its technology. Quibi seeks a declaration that it did not infringe.

events.title: Launch
events.text: The app goes live in North America with a 90-day free trial and a free year for some T-Mobile customers. It reaches No. 3 in Apple’s App Store.

events.title: “1.7 million downloads”
events.text: Whitman tells CNBC the first week beat expectations and that the company will speed up work on casting to televisions.

events.title: “I attribute everything that has gone wrong to coronavirus”
events.text: Katzenberg to the New York Times. Sensor Tower estimates 2.9 million installs; Quibi says 3.5 million, with 1.3 million active users.

events.title: AirPlay support
events.text: Seven weeks after launch, iPhone users can send shows to a television. Chromecast is promised for June.

events.title: Executives take a 10% pay cut
events.text: The company also plans to cut $300 million from first-year content and marketing budgets, the Wall Street Journal reports.

events.title: The Journal publishes the gap
events.text: A reported target of 7.4 million paying subscribers in year one; a pace that would deliver fewer than 2 million. Advertisers are asking to renegotiate.

events.title: No. 284 in the App Store
events.text: Down from No. 3 on launch day. Vulture reports it fell to No. 1,477 when marketing was paused.

events.title: The first free trials expire
events.text: Sensor Tower estimates that 72,000 of the first 910,000 sign-ups became paying subscribers. Quibi says the estimate is “incorrect by an order of magnitude.”

events.title: Judge refuses to switch Turnstyle off
events.text: Eko’s request for a preliminary injunction is denied and three of its nine claims are dismissed; the patent and trade-secret claims go on.

events.title: Ten Emmy nominations
events.text: All in the short-form categories.

events.title: Two Emmys
events.text: Laurence Fishburne and Jasmine Cephas Jones win the short-form acting awards for #FreeRayshawn.

events.title: Strategic options
events.text: The Wall Street Journal reports Quibi is exploring a sale, a new fundraising or a merger with a special-purpose acquisition company.

events.title: Television apps, at last
events.text: Apps for Apple TV, Android TV and Fire TV are released.

events.title: Wind-down announced
events.text: Katzenberg and Whitman publish an open letter: the company will close, sell its content and technology, and return cash to shareholders.

events.title: The app goes dark
events.text: Quibi’s support page had said streaming would end “on or about December 1, 2020.”

events.title: Roku buys the shows
events.text: Roku acquires the content rights, more than 75 shows. The price is not disclosed; it is reported as under $100 million.

events.title: Relaunched as Roku Originals
events.text: The shows return free, with advertising, on The Roku Channel.

events.title: Eight Emmy nominations, for Roku
events.text: Former Quibi shows including Reno 911!, Die Hart and Mapleworth Murders are nominated under their new owner.

events.title: Eko gets Turnstyle
events.text: QBI Holdings and Eko drop all claims. The Turnstyle technology and its intellectual property are transferred to Eko.
